clue.text: Draw small sailing boat

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An instruction to draw a picture of a little yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something roughly is to make a quick outline picture of it, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: A few cut? Everyone's cut!

indicators.note: the second cut trims the word for everyone, chopping off its final letter

blocks.note: to sever is to cut through
everyone is all of them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether only a handful are losing their jobs, and is told the whole staff is going.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'cut' plays two roles: first it is a synonym, then it is the instruction to shorten the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, which is exactly what 'a few' expresses as a quantity.

clue.text: Almost beheaded at dawn?

indicators.note: losing a head means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: almost and nearly are synonyms

explanation.surface: A grim near-execution scheduled for daybreak, the traditional hour for such things.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the start of the day, so something happening then is happening at an early hour; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Space shuttle leaving base for difficult task

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom letter, and leaving it means dropping that final letter

blocks.note: Challenger was one of NASA's space shuttles

explanation.surface: A shuttle leaving its launch base is undertaking something hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as a launch site but means the bottom letter of the word in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a demanding undertaking that tests one's ability, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Student is barred from entire contest

indicators.note: someone barred from a place is kept out, so this letter is removed from the longer word

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate
entire and complete are synonyms

explanation.surface: A student disqualified from taking part in a whole competition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to contest is to fight or vie for something, which is what competing means.

clue.text: Link continued briefly to have an effect

blocks.note: CONT is the usual abbreviation for continued
a drug acts when it has an effect

explanation.surface: A connection kept up for a short while in order to make an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact and link both mean a connection between people, or to get in touch.

clue.text: Avoiding indecency but ultimately lacking manners

indicators.note: lacking what comes ultimately means the word is missing its final letter

blocks.note: a modest person avoids anything indecent

explanation.surface: Someone who is prim but has no real social graces.
explanation.definitionFit: Modes are ways or styles of doing things, so manners in the sense of methods.

clue.text: Genders at variance, no longer friendly

indicators.note: variance is difference or change, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Men and women in disagreement have fallen out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At variance' reads as one phrase, but the AT belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged describes people who were once close but have become distant or hostile.

clue.text: Wayward queen's tirade

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
a tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: A monarch's angry outburst described as wild and erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, which is what wayward behaviour does.

clue.text: Quick-thinking doctor jumps into river

indicators.note: jumping into something puts it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the Nile is the African river
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An alert medic dives into a river to save someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble can describe a mind as well as a body: agile, quick to grasp things.

clue.text: To Iran via Barking, for a change

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Travel directions to Iran by way of Barking, the London suburb, just to do something different.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also a place in east London, which makes the route sound plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A variation is an alteration or departure from the usual, a direct synonym for a change.

clue.text: Discourage TV serial killer, withholding kiss

indicators.note: withholding something means keeping it back, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: Dexter Morgan is the serial killer in the TV series Dexter
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Putting off a television murderer by refusing him a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage them from acting, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Hodgson has a side, which is magnificent!

blocks.note: Roy Hodgson is a former England football manager
taken as written
left, abbreviated L, is a side

explanation.surface: A football manager has assembled a team, and it is a wonderful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a football team, which suits a manager, but here it is just the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal is used loosely to mean splendid or fit for a monarch, hence magnificent.

clue.text: Sailor undoing a satin bow

indicators.note: undoing a knotted thing loosens it, so the letters come apart and re-form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman untying a silky ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain is a ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew, so a kind of seaman.

clue.text: Permit freedom for poet

blocks.note: first meaning: an official document giving permission
second meaning: the liberty a writer takes with rules, as in the poetic phrase

explanation.surface: Granting a poet artistic liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a formal permit and the poetic kind, the freedom to bend rules of grammar or fact.

clue.text: It holds things ancient or new

indicators.note: making something new remakes it, so the letters are put together afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A box that stores items, whether old or recent ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient or new' reads as a contrast pair, but 'or' is part of the letters and 'new' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A container is described by its function: a vessel or box whose purpose is to hold things.

clue.text: Sailor returned to invade African nation that is an island

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
an invader goes inside a country, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: Togo is a West African country
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home and attacks a country, which turns out to be an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the Caribbean island paired with Trinidad in one nation.

clue.text: Rude picture showing model

blocks.note: blue jokes or films are rude ones
a print is a picture

explanation.surface: An indecent photo featuring a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a person posing for the picture, but it means a plan or template.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a design plan, and figuratively a model or template for something else to follow.

clue.text: Concentrating on camping?

blocks.note: first meaning: focused, determined
second meaning, read as two words: someone camping is inside canvas

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about focusing on a camping trip; split the answer as IN TENT and it describes being on a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent as an adjective means absorbed or focused, while split it describes someone lodged under canvas.

clue.text: Poorly pirates walk wearily

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sick buccaneers trudging along tiredly.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge or tramp about in a tired or reluctant way.

clue.text: Shake when stomach is pumped and milk is found in it

indicators.note: a pumped stomach is emptied of its contents, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of stomach
a cow's udder is where milk is held

explanation.surface: A queasy account of having a stomach pumped and milk discovered inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk is found in it' sounds like more of the stomach story, but it is a cryptic description of an udder, which simply follows the emptied stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A shudder is a convulsive tremble, so shake is a synonym as noun or verb.

clue.text: Agent crossing river flowing backwards fast

indicators.note: a river flowing backwards runs the wrong way, so its name is read from end to start
the agent spans across the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A secret agent wading over a fast-flowing river that runs the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy and fast are direct synonyms meaning quick.

clue.text: Answer one puts on internet during scripture

indicators.note: during means within a span, so these pieces go inside the scripture letters

blocks.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
the Roman numeral for one
to post is to put something online

explanation.surface: Someone posting online while a scripture lesson is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, so a kind of retort or answer.

clue.text: Take ages to fit in

blocks.note: how long something will take is how long it will be
to take ages is to be long about it

explanation.surface: It can take a long time to settle in somewhere new.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to feel at home in a group or place, which is to fit in.

clue.text: Revolutionary Basques steal beer? Fancy!

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

blocks.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
to rob is to steal
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: Basque militants pinching beer, and someone asks if you would like some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sounds like a description of the militants, but it turns all three pieces round together.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, fancy and elaborate both mean ornate or intricate, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Nixon in China perhaps seeing first half of military manoeuvres

indicators.note: keeping only the first half means the back half of the word is thrown away

blocks.note: military manoeuvres are operations

explanation.surface: A former US president visiting China and observing army exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Nixon in China is John Adams's opera about the 1972 visit, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nixon in China is a well-known modern opera, given as an example of the genre.

clue.text: Choose to be chubby

blocks.note: first meaning: to opt for it
second meaning: rounded and fleshy

explanation.surface: Deciding to put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to opt decisively, and the adjective means pleasantly rounded or fat.

clue.text: Dupe and depose leaders and cause huge change

indicators.note: deposing a leader removes them from the top, so each word loses its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plot to trick and overthrow those in charge, bringing upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depose leaders' reads as a political coup but simply removes the first letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend things is to turn them upside down, figuratively to transform them radically.

clue.text: Doorman skinned cat

indicators.note: skinning strips the outside away, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: a bouncer guards the door of a club

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman who flayed a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Dessert, alcohol and feasts regularly causing slight corpulence

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert
gin is an alcoholic spirit
the second, fourth and sixth letters of feasts

explanation.surface: Puddings, drink and regular banquets leading to a bit of a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudginess is a slight plumpness, a mild form of being fat.

clue.text: Rubbish initially bunged in outbuilding

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it
in places that letter inside the building

blocks.note: a garage is an outbuilding for a car
the first letter of bunged

explanation.surface: Junk dumped in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunged' is British slang for chucked carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage and rubbish both mean waste material to be thrown away.

clue.text: Section of Liebestod — generally heavy stuff

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from something longer, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the next

explanation.surface: A passage from Wagner's Liebestod, the ponderous love-death aria, is generally hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: Liebestod is the final aria of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food, and by extension dull, heavy-going material.
